nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: What is the target area for mangrove expansion in Pakistan?
nodes.answer: The target area for mangrove expansion in Pakistan is 865,000 acres.
nodes.paragraph: Since then, mangroves have expanded to 593,0 acres, with a target of 865,0 acres (Khan 2024). This success is attributed to initiatives like the Green Pakistan Program, Billion Tree Tsunami, and Ten-Billion Tree Tsu- nami (Saeed et al. 2019). Pakistan set Guinness World Records in 2009 and 2013 for planting over half a million and 850,0 mangrove saplings in a single day, respec- tively (Mahar et al. 2020). Currently, Pakistan features the largest dry-climate mangrove forest in the world, covering an area of 600,0 hectares that surrounds the Indus Delta (Bindiya et al. 2023; Laghari et al. 2015). The Sindh Forest Department manages one of the world S largest mangrove reserves, ranking as the seventh-largest globally, highlighting a significant conservation initiative in Pakistan (Laghari et al. 2015) ). Pakistan S coastline stretches 1050 km (652 miles) across the Sindh and Baluchistan provinces, with the majority of it located in Baluchistan.
